Part 1: Examples made with GenAI
Audit Trail Assessment Toolkit
A guide to designing assessments where students record what they did and why, not just the final product.
Physical trail: the actions students take, such as searches, sources and AI used.
Intellectual trail: the reasoning behind them.
By Haider Ali, Dorottya Sallai, Luc Schneider, Hera Stamatiou and Lucrezia Zito. Hosted on Lovable.
audittrailtoolkit.lovable.app
An audit trail builder for a Marketing Management assessment

Planning tools for students
Assessment and term planner 2026/27
Brings students’ courses, assessment deadlines, weightings and timetable into one week-by-week planner for the term, saved to their account.
Hosted on Lovable

Assessment tracker
Helps students plan revision around their exams and deadlines, with a daily schedule, a focus timer and a countdown to each exam.

Part 2: Your turn
Use GenAI to make learning resources you can keep
Dr Dori Sallai
Department of Management
Steven Williams
Eden Centre and Digital Skills Lab
What you’ll make today
Interactive web pages and animated videos for your students.
You don’t need any coding experience: you describe what you want, and Claude writes the code.
The Disciplinary Atlas, made with Claude by Dr Chris Blunt for LSE100 and uploaded to Moodle as a single HTML file.
Make once, use anywhere
Portable files
You can keep and use files where ever you want: HTML files for interactive activities, and MP4, GIF and PDF files for visual explainers.
No Claude account needed
Students open your resources on Moodle or a free hosting site, with or without a Claude licence.
No platform lock-in
The skills you practise, such as giving context, asking for a plan and testing the result, work the same way in any GenAI tool.

Prepare your materials
Step 1
Decide which files to add
Three to five files from one course, for example:
  • your course outline, with the topic for each week
  • the slides or notes for one week
  • a case study or seminar task
  • notes on what students find difficult
Step 2
Put copies in a Project folder
Make a folder on your computer, for example in OneDrive. It’s your master copy: add or edit files here first, then in Claude.
Step 3
Prepare each file for its type
Images essential? Keep it as a PDF, so Claude can see the images.
Everything else: convert it to Markdown with deskmark (bit.ly/deskmark) and save it in your folder.
2
Worksheet screen 2 – Prepare your materials
How Claude reads your files
Everything in memory
While the files are small enough, Claude reads all of them in every chat. They sit in its context window, so it can connect ideas across your whole course.
Search mode
Once the files grow too large, Claude looks up the snippets that seem most relevant, and can miss context elsewhere. PDFs are the usual cause.
A Project of PDFs in Search mode at 10% of capacity.
9
Worksheet screen 9 – How Claude reads your files
What is Markdown?
A way of showing formatting in plain text. A few punctuation marks you can see do the job of Word’s hidden formatting codes.
What the file contains
# Week 3: Leading change **Kotter’s eight steps** begin with: - Create a sense of urgency - Build a guiding coalition
What it means
Week 3: Leading change
Kotter’s eight steps begin with:
  • Create a sense of urgency
  • Build a guiding coalition

Worksheet screen 2 – Prepare your materials
Your Project instructions do three jobs
Describe your course
The course, the students and the topic for each week, so resources match where students are.
Set how Claude works with you
Base content on your materials, flag anything added, ask questions one at a time and show a plan first.
Set rules for every resource
One self-contained HTML file, no storage or AI features, accessible, and tested in a browser before you see it.

Worksheet screen 3 – Set up your Project
Your turn: choose your activity
Activity A
5
Screen 5
A revision activity
Students practise concepts from several weeks, mixed together, and explain their answer before they see it.
Learning principle: interleaving and retrieval practice
Activity B
6
Screen 6
A map of your course
Students explore how concepts connect, explaining each one in their own words before they see the definition.
Learning principle: connecting new ideas to earlier ones
Activity C
7
Screen 7
An animated explainer video
Students watch a concept from your course build up step by step.
Learning principle: words next to pictures, built up in stages
Making a video? Tips for Activity C
How it works
Claude draws each scene with code and joins the frames into an MP4. Rendering takes several minutes, so aim to get as far as the storyboard and preview stills today.
Works well
Flat shapes, diagrams, pictograms and text: processes, models and frameworks
Works poorly
Realistic people, detailed illustration and charts of real data

Skills to take with you
Skill
What it means in any GenAI tool
Give it context
Start from your own materials and course sequence.
Use plain-text files
Markdown takes little space, and you can see what the tool sees.
Ask for a plan before a build
Have the tool ask you questions and show you the content first.
Check what it makes
Compare it with your materials and test it as a student would.
Keep the files
Download what you make and host it yourself.
